|url-status=dead }} 1981) is a Greek professional [[basketball]] player for [[Ilysiakos B.C.|Ilysiakos]]. His height is of {{convert|2.09|m|adj=on|frac=4}} tall. During his professional career he was also the [[captain (sports)|captain]] of the senior [[Greece men's national basketball team|Greek national team]]. In most of his playing career, he played primarily as a [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]], but he could also sometimes be used as a small ball [[center (basketball)|center]], or even as a [[small forward]], if needed. Fotsis was inducted into the [[Greek Basket League Hall of Fame]] in 2022. ==Professional career== ===Europe=== Born in [[Maroussi]], [[Athens]], Fotsis began his career as one of the biggest European prospects. Fotsis began his professional career in 1996, with the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] club [[Ilysiakos B.C.|Ilysiakos]]. He quickly earned a reputation as a very talented young player when playing in the club's senior team. He then transferred to the Greek club [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] (PAO) in 1997, just at the age of sixteen. It is a fact of significant importance that he started his career as a [[point guard]], and later moved to the [[small forward]], and then [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] positions. Due to his early guard playing status, he was later always recognized as one of the best power forwards in Europe, regarding basketball technique. While being the most dominant-youth aged talent in Greece at the time, he twice participated in the [[Nike Hoop Summit]] All-World Team (1998, 1999). He got little playing time in his first two seasons with Panathinaikos, but he managed to become one of the team's key players during the 1999–00 season. With Panathinaikos, he won the [[EuroLeague]] championship that same season, while being barely nineteen. One year later, he became a starter on the Panathinaikos team that made it to the [[FIBA SuproLeague]]'s [[2001 FIBA SuproLeague Final Four|Finals]]. ===NBA=== Fotsis was selected by the [[Vancouver Grizzlies]] (who were relocated to Memphis right after the draft) in the 2nd round (48th overall) of the [[2001 NBA draft]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/draft2001/news/draft_order.html |title=NBA Draft 2001 |work=nba.com |access-date=2011-01-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110210143314/http://www.nba.com/draft2001/news/draft_order.html |archive-date=February 10, 2011 |url-status=dead }} In his one and only season in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], he appeared in 28 games for the Grizzlies during the [[2001–02 NBA season]], averaging 3.9 points and 2.2 rebounds per game. He scored a career high 21 points against the [[Orlando Magic]] on January 19, 2002. His final NBA game was on April 17, 2002, in a 94–109 loss to the [[Seattle SuperSonics]], in which he recorded 10 points and 6 rebounds. ===Return to Europe=== After spending the [[2001–02 NBA season|2001–02 season]] in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], he returned to Panathinaikos for the 2002–03 season, and became one of the team's leaders, while scoring an average of 14.5 points per game in [[EuroLeague]]. With PAO, he won both the [[Greek Basketball Cup|Greek Cup]] and the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] championship that year. In 2003, he moved to the [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]] club [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]]. With Real Madrid, he was one of the key contributors on the teams that made it to the [[ULEB Cup|EuroCup]] Finals in 2004, and won the [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]] championship in 2005. In 2005, he then transferred to the [[Russian Basketball Super League 1|Russian Superleague]] club [[MBC Dynamo Moscow|Dynamo Moscow]]. With Dynamo Moscow, Fotsis was one of the two leaders of the Russian team, along with fellow Greek player [[Lazaros Papadopoulos]]. Fotsis won the EuroCup championship in 2006 with Dynamo. One year later, he reached the EuroLeague quarterfinals with Dynamo, where his team lost to Panathinaikos. On March 21, 2007, in a winner-take-all [[2006–07 Euroleague|EuroLeague 2006–07 season]] showdown with [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]] power [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Benetton Treviso]], for second place in [[Euroleague 2006-07 Top 16 Group F|their Top 16 group]], and a place in the quarterfinals, Fotsis scored 22 points, and set a single-game [[EuroLeague]] [[Euroleague records since the 2000–01 season|post year 2000 record]] with 24 rebounds, helping Dynamo score a 68-65 [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] win.{{Cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/10164/180/item |title=Dynamo's Fotsis breaks all-time rebounds record! |publisher=Euroleague |date=March 21, 2007}} In 2008, he returned to Panathinaikos. It was his second return to the club, and he was in the starting lineup for the team, as they won the coveted [[European Basketball Triple Crown|Triple Crown]] during the 2008–09 season. Fotsis was a key contributor to the Triple Crown winners, with his good defensive play and clutch baskets. He also played more minutes than any other "Greens" player in the [[2009 EuroLeague Final Four]]. In the 2009–10 season, Panathinaikos again won the Greek League championship. That same season, Fotsis was named the Greek League [[Most valuable player|MVP]] for the month of April. He played more minutes than any other "Greens" player in the EuroLeague that season, showing his defensive skills as well.[http://esake.gr/article/14049 ESAKE.gr - COSMOTE MVP Απριλίου ο Φώτσης {{in lang|el}}.] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100507100830/http://esake.gr/article/14049 |date=May 7, 2010 }} In July 2011, he signed with [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Olimpia Milano]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]], for two seasons.[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/86392/180/aj-milano-puts-fotsis-at-forward AJ Milano puts Fotsis at forward.] On July 2, 2013, [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] announced that they had signed Fotsis for three seasons.[http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2013-14-signings/i/114654/8177/panathinaikos-athens-brings-back-fotsis Euroleague.net PANATHINAIKOS ATHENS brings back Fotsis.] In 2016, Fotsis signed a new two-year contract with Panathinaikos.{{Cite news|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/en/featured/268153/fotsis-ready-to-sign-a-new-two-year-deal-with-panathinaikos/|title=Fotsis ready to sign a new two year deal with Panathinaikos - Eurohoops|date=2016-06-25|newspaper=Eurohoops|access-date=2017-02-19|language=en-US}} On July 25, 2017, he parted ways with Panathinaikos.{{cite news|title=Panathinaikos BC Superfoods Announcement|url=http://www.paobc.gr/page.ashx?pid=2&aid=44625&lang=2|access-date=25 July 2017|work=paobc.gr|date=25 July 2017}} In August 2017, he announced his return to [[Ilysiakos B.C.|Ilysiakos]], the first team of his professional career back in 1996.[https://www.sport24.gr/basket/stin-a-eska-o-fotsis-epistrefei-ston-ilisiako/ Στην Α' ΕΣΚΑ ο Φώτσης: Επιστρέφει στον Ηλυσιακό!], sport24.gr. 2 August 2017. (in Greek) ==National team career== [[Image:Antonis Fotis Greece (cropped).jpg|right|thumb|120px|Fotsis, as a member of the senior [[Greece men's national basketball team]].]] With the junior national team of Greece, Fotsis won the bronze medal at the [[1998 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]]. He played with the senior men's [[Greece men's national basketball team|Greek national team]] at the [[2009 EuroBasket]], and the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Summer Olympics]]. He was also a member of the Greek men's national teams that won the gold medal at the [[2005 EuroBasket]] and the silver medal at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]]. He also played at the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympics]], and he became the [[Captain (sports)|captain]] of Greece's senior national team before the [[2009 EuroBasket]] tournament, where Greece won the bronze medal. He was also a member of the Greek men's national teams that played at the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]], the [[2011 EuroBasket]], the [[2012 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament for Men|2012 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament]], and the [[2013 EuroBasket]]. He is the 7th all-time leading scorer of the Greek senior men's national team, with 1,734 points scored in his career (9.4 points per game).[http://www.basket.gr/index.php/playerview?playerid=171 ΦΩΤΣΗΣ ΑΝΤΩΝΗΣ {{in lang|el}}.] ==Personal life== Fotsis has had the nickname of "[[Batman]]" since his adolescent years, when his teammates in the Greek junior national teams named him after the well-known comic-strip figure, because of his ability at that age to be an overwhelmingly gliding presence above the basketball rim.[http://www.euroleague.net/final-four/berlin-2009/main-page/i/48829/2772/item Euroleague.net Spanoulis interview.] In his prime, Fotsis was a [[Block (basketball)|shot blocker]], an offensive [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounder]], and an excellent [[Three-point field goal|3-point shooter]], especially for a [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]]. He was also physical on the defensive end of the court, thanks to his athleticism. He also holds Turkish citizenship.[http://www.ntv.com.tr/spor/yunan-milli-takimi-kaptani-turkiye-vatandasi-oldu%2cStVdziJsq0e_HMZYFGEm_w Fotsis became Turkish citizen.] ==Career statistics==
